description: Re-renders one bad segment of a finished MiniMax-H3 chain in place and splices it back, so the rest of the take is kept rather than re-rolled (#1169). The chain must have been run with 'save_segments' and 'keep_segments' on its chain block, which leave each segment as a playable mp4 beside the take; 'chain_output' is an 'output:' reference to any one of those files (<prefix>.<n>.segment-000.mp4) and the rest are found beside it. 'segment' is 1-based and must be an interior one, 2 to N-1: the first segment has nothing before it and the last nothing after it, so both need a one-sided repair this template does not make, and are refused. 'chain_repair_cut' counts the segment files and cuts the guides: the repair is one fl2va render with segment k-1's last 'head_frames' frames held at frame 0 (its first frame is the keyframe, as a guide chain gives its own segments) and segment k+1's frames held as a guide ending at the render's last frame, both with their audio, so picture and soundtrack run on from one neighbour into the other. A guide starts on the 17-frame grid and a render is 17n + 5 frames, so the frames between the guides number 12 more than a multiple of 17 while an interior segment of a 124/22 chain is 102: the new frames replace segment k and the first 12 frames of segment k+1, the tail guide is segment k+1's frames from 12 on, and the splice takes segment k+1 back from frame 12. 'num_frames' is the render's length - at least 'head_frames' + the segment's frames + 'tail_frames', rounded up onto the grid; the default 175 fits an interior segment of the chained-segments defaults (124 frames, guide_frames 22) with the 22/39 holds, and a value too small is refused before the model loads, naming the one to pass. The tail hold outnumbers the head hold by default (39 against 22). After the render the guide spans are trimmed off picture and audio ('trim_video') and 'concat_videos' with 'continuous_joins' joins segments 1..k-1, the repair and segments k+1..N: the take keeps its frame count exactly, and its two repaired seams are recorded as continuous rather than as cuts, so 'analyze_seams' measures their frame jump as it measures the chain's own seams. Every other frame is the segment files' own, through one more h264 encode, not byte-identical. Pass the chain's own settings: its canvas ('width'/'height', checked against the segment files), steps, shifts, LoRA, weights_dtype and its counters ('guide_noise'; 'latent_anchor', an 'output:' of segment 1's file, for a chain run with anchor segment_1), since a workflow cannot read another run's workflow - the defaults are the chained-segments template's. The text encoder and its truncation are the chain's. 'seed' defaults to a new one: a re-render at the chain's seed would not redraw the segment's noise anyway, since a chain runs one generator through every segment. 'prompt' should describe this segment's stretch of the take, timed for the render's length. Concepts only from H3MD Director and roycho87/geiru_context_suite (docs/ATTRIBUTIONS.md).
summary: Re-render one interior segment of a finished H3 chain between its neighbours and splice it back.

vram_estimate.reason: one H3 render: the t2va calibration (#324) - peak activation memory scales with width * height * num_frames at 28.71 bytes a voxel - plus its two guides, each encoded on the target canvas at about the clip's own cost per voxel (docs/proposals/h3-guide-vram.md, #694). The guides are clips cut at run time, which the per-guide charge cannot count before the run and would price at num_frames each, so their frames are folded into the voxel rate instead: 28.71 * (175 + 22 + 39) / 175 = 38.72 bytes, exact at the default 175-frame render with the 22/39 holds and slightly over for a longer render with the same holds

variables.prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Cinematic, live-action macro photography with a shallow depth of field, one continuous shot. The shot opens exactly on <Picture 1>: a translucent blown glass figure fills the frame against a dark, softly graded background, its surface catching cool rim light along every curve and throwing small caustics onto the surface beneath it. Its tentacles writhe without pause, curling and uncurling in slow deliberate coils, the glass flexing as though molten while staying perfectly clear. The figure (S1), a deep cavernous male voice with a long tail of reverb, unhurried and very low in pitch, speaks steadily throughout, <d>[English] Rise now. The old ones are listening.</d> Its central mass swells and contracts with the cadence of the words, and the caustics on the surface below ripple in time. The camera holds a static shot, letting the tentacles move through the frame edges.

overall_soundscape: A dark, near-silent room tone under a faint low-frequency hum. The tentacle movement carries a fine, dry glass-on-glass squeak and an occasional soft chime as two limbs touch, continuous and unhurried from the first frame to the last.

non_diegetic_music: A sustained low drone of bowed double bass and detuned synthesiser, almost subsonic, holding an even intensity with no discernible melody or pulse.

num_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and MiniMax-H3 generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps

segment.reason: segment 1 has no segment before it to hold - repairing the first segment (or the last) needs a one-sided repair with one guide, which this template does not make; the last segment is refused when the run counts the chain's files

width.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for

height.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
